discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 8fcdf49. The encoded PowerShell probe now exits non-zero when its working directory is a `\\wsl$` / `\\wsl.localhost` UNC path, so a WSL endpoint (where `powershell.exe` is reachable through interop) is rejected and falls through to the POSIX probe instead of being accepted as Windows.

Fixed in 807892c0. Your mounted-drive concern was valid: I reproduced the old probe reporting `herdr-windows:AMD64` from WSL `/mnt/c` while `uname` reported Linux.

The cwd heuristic is removed. The first probe now checks expansion in the SSH login shell before accepting Windows PowerShell's result. Ordinary fallback probes use the same guard; only an explicit MINGW/MSYS/Cygwin uname hint permits the direct Windows probe.

Live sh/bash/zsh probes reject Windows from both `/home` and `/mnt/c`; native Windows PowerShell 5/7 and cmd probes succeed with empty stderr. The new native Windows regression test executes the same Windows PowerShell binary through native and POSIX login shells. Full Windows `just check` and 69 focused WSL checks passed.

Addressed in `1d06f67f`. The test now bounds both kernel socket buffers — `SO_SNDBUF` on the writer and `SO_RCVBUF` on the observer — to 64 KiB via `limit_local_stream_buffers`, which is far below the 1 MiB frame. The writer must therefore block for the observer and can only finish by resetting its deadline across many drains, independent of the platform default buffer sizes.

The shell intentionally becomes Online after a fresh snapshot in `install_client_shell_snapshot` (`src/client/shell_runtime.rs`), or after the active presentation fence commits. A successful handshake alone does not make a coherent screen ready for pane input. That snapshot path calls `set_endpoint_status(Online)`, which clears the diagnostic and retry marker. Moving it into `Connected` would bypass the existing readiness boundary. I’m keeping that boundary intact; an attempt waiting for its initial snapshot remains in progress under this PR’s stated scope.

Thanks. This SSH host is already the trusted execution peer and can send an unbounded stream after the marker as well. A preamble cap would therefore not establish a resource boundary; it would only reject a new, unevidenced class of remote profiles. The parser keeps at most one discarded line, and the concrete profile-noise failure this framing fixes is covered by the live Windows SSH test. We are keeping the reader minimal under the repository rule against speculative limits.

You were right that the previous `read_until` implementation buffered an unbounded line before the marker; my earlier stream comparison missed that distinction. The updated head replaces it with one shared, constant-state `BufRead::fill_buf`/`consume` scanner for POSIX and Windows startup output. It accepts banners of arbitrary length, handles markers split across read buffers, and preserves all bytes after the marker without retaining the preamble. Captured setup output uses the same framing after the existing process capture.

@ogulcancelik The extra round trip is real, but I think it is the right tradeoff here. The check must happen immediately before each API operation: caching once per CLI process would reopen the exact stale-server gap if an install/handoff replaces the server between `plugin.list` and `plugin.link`. A wait subscription is pinged once before it opens, not once per event, and these are bounded local socket/pipe round trips. I would not weaken or cache this without measured latency showing a problem. If it does become material, the clean optimization is same-connection protocol negotiation/dispatch, not skipping per-operation validation.
